 Shopee affiliate program drives sales growth for Filipino MSMEs 
 Close menu 
 November 4, 2026 
 7:05AM PHT
 E-Commerce 
 Shopee 
 Share
 Insider Spotlight 
 Shopee reported more than 1.5 times growth in affiliate-driven traffic and sales, highlighting the growing role of creator-led commerce 
 Filipino brands Herah, Hyperbrands and B Coffee Co. are using affiliate partnerships to reach customers and improve product visibility 
 Shopee held more than 30 KOLLAB events in 2026, connecting over 100 brands with more than 500 creators and affiliates 
 Filipino micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are increasingly turning to affiliate marketing to expand their customer reach and drive online sales, as creator-led commerce gains traction in the country's e-commerce sector.
 Shopee reported that affiliate-driven traffic and sales on its platform grew by more than 1.5 times, reflecting how businesses are using content creators to introduce products to potential customers and convert online engagement into purchases. 
 For smaller businesses with limited marketing budgets, affiliate partnerships offer another way to reach targeted audiences without relying solely on traditional advertising. 
 Through Shopee's Affiliate Program, sellers can work with creators who demonstrate products, share personal experiences and direct shoppers to purchase within the platform. 
 For MSMEs, the program offers another way to reach potential customers and discover creators whose audiences match their products. For creators, it offers a genuine wayto earn. | Contributed photo 
 For experimenting, exploring brands 
 Homegrown innerwear brand Herah used affiliate-generated videos to demonstrate its products, including a practical tutorial on cleaning nipple covers that helped drive sales. 
 The company subsequently established a dedicated team to manage creator partnerships and monitor content performance. 
 Meanwhile, Hyperbrands, which operates pet-care brands Dentalight and Moochie, uses Shopee's performance data to evaluate affiliate content and refine its marketing approach. 
 “Those moments remind us that there is always more to learn. Even when we think we have found a winning approach, creators bring fresh ideas that encourage us to keep experimenting and exploring,” Hyperbrands CEO  Luis Gan  said in a press statement. 
 Creator partnerships 
 Filipino-owned B Coffee Co. also uses affiliate content to demonstrate how its coffee machines fit into everyday routines, helping customers better understand its products before purchasing. 
 The brand has participated in Shopee's KOLLAB initiative to establish additional creator partnerships. 
 In 2026, Shopee organized more than 30 KOLLAB events involving over 100 brands and 500 creators and affiliates, including activities in Cebu and Davao. 
 Shopee plans to expand access to affiliate partnerships beyond Metro Manila, connecting more provincial businesses with local creators. 
 "Through our Affiliate Program and initiatives like KOLLAB, we're making it easier for MSMEs to connect with the right creators and turn content into real business results. We'll keep investing to make these opportunities accessible to more businesses and creators across the country," Shopee Philippines head of commercial  Jack Ng  said. —Vanessa Hidalgo | Ed: Corrie S.
